title: Heated panel frequency response
line: A thermal-stress FEA study of a clamped titanium heat-shield panel heated 150 K and driven by exhaust noise.
description: Forced vibration of a titanium heat-shield panel (200 x 200 x 6 mm) beside an engine exhaust, clamped on its four edges and running 150 K above its fitting temperature. The in-plane compression lowers its natural frequencies. A thermal step, a preload, a prestressed modal step and a modal frequency sweep from 500 Hz to 1.6 kHz return the hot modes and the response to a uniform 1 kPa of exhaust noise.
thumbnailAlt: Hot titanium panel vibrating in its first mode under exhaust noise, solved in RunMat
